You can find **olive oil** in various places, depending on your location and preferences. Here are the best places to look:

### **1. Grocery Stores & Supermarkets**
   - **Large chains** (Walmart, Kroger, Safeway, Publix, Albertsons, etc.)
   - **Organic/health-focused stores** (Whole Foods, Sprouts, Trader Joe’s, Natural Grocers)
   - **International markets** (Middle Eastern, Italian, Greek, or Spanish grocery stores often carry high-quality olive oil)

### **2. Specialty & Gourmet Stores**
   - **Olive oil boutiques** (stores specializing in high-end olive oils, often with tasting options)
   - **Cheese & wine shops** (many carry premium olive oils)
   - **Farmers' markets** (local producers often sell fresh, unfiltered olive oil)

### **3. Online Retailers**
   - **Amazon** (wide selection, but check reviews for authenticity)
   - **Specialty olive oil websites** (e.g., [Brightland](https://brightland.co/), [Kasandrinos](https://www.kasandrinos.com/), [California Olive Ranch](https://www.californiaoliveranch.com/))
   - **Etsy** (for small-batch, artisanal olive oils)
   - **International sellers** (e.g., [La Tienda](https://www.tienda.com/) for Spanish olive oil, [Greek Internet Market](https://www.greekinternetmarket.com/) for Greek varieties)

### **4. Bulk & Warehouse Stores**
   - **Costco, Sam’s Club, BJ’s Wholesale** (often carry large bottles at good prices)
   - **Restaurant supply stores** (if you need bulk quantities)

### **5. Direct from Producers (Best for Freshness & Quality)**
   - **Olive oil farms & mills** (many offer online ordering or local pickup)
   - **Farmers' co-ops** (especially in olive-growing regions like California, Italy, Spain, Greece, or Turkey)
   - **Subscription services** (some companies deliver fresh olive oil seasonally)

### **6. Discount & Dollar Stores (Budget Option)**
   - **Dollar General, Aldi, Lidl, Grocery Outlet** (may have affordable but lower-quality options)

### **Tips for Buying Olive Oil:**
✅ **Check the label** – Look for **"Extra Virgin Olive Oil" (EVOO)** for the highest quality.
✅ **Harvest date** – Fresher is better (ideally within **12–18 months**).
✅ **Origin** – Single-origin (e.g., Italy, Spain, Greece, California) is often better than blended oils.
✅ **Dark glass or tin containers** – Protects from light degradation.
❌ **Avoid "light" or "pure" olive oil** – These are refined and lower quality.
❌ **Beware of fake olive oil** – Some cheap brands dilute with other oils; stick to trusted brands or certified sources (e.g., **COOC, NAOOA, or EU PDO/PGI labels**).

### **Best Brands to Look For (By Quality Tier):**
| **Premium (High-End)** | **Mid-Range (Good Quality)** | **Budget (Affordable)** |
|------------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------|
| **Brightland** (USA) | **California Olive Ranch** | **Bertolli (EVOO)** |
| **Kasandrinos** (Greece) | **Filippo Berio** | **Colavita** |
| **Castillo de Canena** (Spain) | **Goya (EVOO)** | **Pompeian** |
| **Frantoio Franci** (Italy) | **Lucini** | **Great Value (Walmart)** |
| **Olio Verde** (Sicily) | **Partanna** | **Aldi Simply Nature** |

Would you like recommendations based on a specific use (cooking, dipping, salad dressings) or region?
